summary: All five repair targets are valid structural edits: pending questions should not embed recommended answers or implementation-level test decisions.

items.title: 1. q1 includes proposed answer/instruction
items.rationale: q1 can be rewritten as a goal confirmation question without embedding the expected answer.
items.evidence: draft.json qa[0].question begins with a recommended must-level statement.

items.title: 2. q2 includes proposed answer/rationale
items.rationale: q2 can ask for the desired observability contract without prescribing the metric shape in the question text.
items.evidence: draft.json qa[1].question includes provider callCount exclusion and cacheHit/cachedResponse wording as the answer.

items.title: 3. q3 includes proposed answer/instruction
items.rationale: q3 can ask about retention needs while leaving the artifact-retention answer open.
items.evidence: draft.json qa[2].question states the active-flow/spec-local retention policy as the proposed answer.

items.title: 4. q4 includes proposed answer/instruction
items.rationale: q4 can ask which unsuccessful response classes must be excluded without embedding the exclusion policy as an answer.
items.evidence: draft.json qa[3].question lists the non-cache policy as a recommended must-level answer.

items.title: 5. q5 asks internal implementation/test details
items.rationale: q5 can be rewritten at acceptance-evidence level instead of asking the user to choose unit or e2e implementation details.
items.evidence: draft.json qa[4].question names unit test and e2e metrics scope, which project test patterns can decide later.
